  JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY
   COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICE
  CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF
 CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY
     EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV
    TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,
    CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,
   MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA,
SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES




                          SOAH ORDER NO. 19
               ORDER GRANTING MOTION TO COMPEL


     On May 13, 2026, Kevin Kennedy filed a motion (Motion) to compel
responses to Requests for Information (RFIs). Mr. Kennedy seeks an order
compelling Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission
Service Corporation (collectively, Applicants) to provide any non-privileged
responsive information to RFI JKK 10-03. Mr. Kennedy also seeks an order
 compelling the staff (Staff) of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission)
to provide responses to Mr. Kennedy’s Sixth RFI.1 Applicants did not file a response
to the Motion. Commission Staff filed a response on May 20, 2026.


        A.       KENNEDY’S TENTH RFI TO APPLICANTS

        JKK 10-03 requests that Applicants “[p]rovide copies of any known written
information, which you may have (motions, orders, decisions, letters, emails,
memos, meeting minutes, etc.) mentioning or regarding consolidation of Bell County
East to Big Hill and Big Hill to Sand Lake 765-kV transmission line projects dated on
or after July 25, 2024. If you do not know of any, just say that you do not know of any
such information.”2 Applicants objected that the RFI seeks information outside the
scope of discovery because under 16 Texas Administrative Code section 22.141(a),
the scope of discovery does not include matters privileged or exempted under the
Texas Rules of Evidence.3 Applicants assert that under Texas Rule of Evidence
503(b), confidential communications between client and counsel for the purpose of
obtaining or providing legal advice are generally insulated from disclosure. To the
extent Mr. Kennedy seeks non-privileged information, Applicants did not object.




1 Kevin Kennedy’s Sixth [RFI] to the Public Utility Commission of Texas, Item 3566 (Apr. 29, 2026).

2 Kevin Kennedy’s Tenth [RFI] to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation, Item 3968 (Apr. 29, 2026) (Kennedy’s Tenth RFI).
3 Objections of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation to [Kennedy’s

Tenth RFI], Item 3703 (May 7, 2026).
                                                        2
                                          SOAH Order No. 19
                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
          The Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) find that the Motion has merit with
respect to Applicants. Applicants are ORDERED to provide non-privileged
information in response to JKK 10-03 by May 28, 2026.


         B.       KENNEDY’S SIXTH RFI TO COMMISSION STAFF

         JKK PUC 06-01 requests Commission Staff provide

         PUC Docket Control Number and Item Number of any known docket
         postings mentioning or regarding consolidation of the Bell County East
         to Big Hill and Big Hill to Sand Lake 765-kV transmission line projects
         that were posted on the date range of July 25, 2024, through January 31,
         2026. If you do not know of any, just say you do not know of any such
         postings.


         JKK PUC 06-02 requests the same information but posted after
January 31, 2026. JKK PUC 06-03 requests

         copies of any known written information (motion, orders, decisions,
         letters, emails, memos, meeting minutes, etc.) mentioning or regarding
         consolidation of the Bell County East to Big Hill and Big Hill to Sand
         Lake 765-kV transmission line projects dated on or after July 25, 2024.
         If you do not know of any, just say that you do not know of any such
         information.


         Staff argues that the requests are unduly burdensome as the discovery can be
obtained from other sources that are more convenient, less burdensome, or less
expensive, including sources that are publicly accessible and available for
Mr. Kennedy’s use to perform his own research.4 Staff also contends that the RFIs


4 See Tex. R. Civ. P. 192.4(a).

                                                      3
                                            SOAH Order No. 19
                              SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
 have been rendered moot by the order partially granting Mr. Kennedy’s motion to
consolidate.5 Additionally, Staff urges that the information exceeds the scope of
discovery because the information is not relevant to the determination under Public
Utility Regulatory Act section 37.056 and 16 Texas Administrative Code section
25.101 regarding whether the projects are needed. Staff also contends that the
information sought is within the possession, custody, or control of the Commission
and not Commission Staff.


        Staff did not explain how the requests were unduly burdensome, and the ALJs
are not convinced that the sources accessible to Mr. Kennedy are more convenient
or less burdensome than those available to Staff. The ALJs find that the consolidation
matter remains relevant to the proceeding as a whole and falls within the scope of
discovery. Moreover, the ALJs are unpersuaded that the requested information is
outside of Staff’s possession or custody.


        Mr. Kennedy’s Motion is GRANTED. Commission Staff is ORDERED to
provide non-privileged information in response to Mr. Kennedy’s Sixth RFI
(including JKK PUC 06-01, 06-02, and 06-03) by May 28, 2026.




5 See SOAH Order No. 12 (May 8, 2026).
